title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 119
paragraphs: This other story, I say, is reported about Xerxes's return, but I myself can in no way believe it — neither in other respects, nor concerning what is said to have happened to the Persians. For if what I have related had truly been said by the pilot to Xerxes, not one person's opinion in ten thousand would differ from mine that the king would have done something like this: he would have made those on deck go down below into the hold, since they were Persians of the highest rank; and of the rowers, who were Phoenicians, he would have thrown into the sea a number equal to the Persians on deck. In fact, however, as I have said before, he returned to Asia together with the rest of the army by road.
